Breaking: SAIR: Accelerating Pharma R&D with AI-Powered Structural Intelligence

📅 02 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1217 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that this summer, SandboxAQ released the Structurally Augmented IC50 Repository (SAIR), the largest dataset of co-folded 3D protein-ligand structures paired with experimentally measured IC₅₀ labels, directly linking molecular structure to drug potency and overcoming a longstanding scarcity in training data.
  • SAIR is an open-sourced dataset and is publicly available for free under a permissive CC BY 4.0 license, making it immediately actionable for commercial and non-commercial R&D pipelines.
  • AI and computer-aided design have great potential in dramatically accelerating the development of fresh drugs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this summer, SandboxAQ released the Structurally Augmented IC50 Repository (SAIR), the largest dataset of co-folded 3D protein-ligand structures paired with experimentally measured IC₅₀ labels, directly linking molecular structure to drug potency and overcoming a longstanding scarcity in training data. This dataset is now available on Hugging Face, and for the first time, researchers have open access to more than 5 million AI‑generated, high‑accuracy protein-ligand 3D structures, each paired with validated empirical binding potency data.

SAIR is an open-sourced dataset and is publicly available for free under a permissive CC BY 4.0 license, making it immediately actionable for commercial and non-commercial R&D pipelines. More than just a dataset, SAIR is a strategic asset that bridges the long-standing data gap in AI-powered drug design. It empowers pharmaceutical, biotech, and tech‑bio leaders to accelerate R&D, expand target horizons, and supercharge AI models – moving more of the costly, lengthy drug design and optimization from the wet lab to in silico. This means shorter hit‑to‑lead timelines, more efficient lead optimization, fewer dead‑end projects, and a more predictable path from initial idea to clinical candidate.

AI and computer-aided design have great potential in dramatically accelerating the development of fresh drugs. For decades, scientists have dreamed about AI that could identify or design a potent, non-toxic, and efficacious compound from a prompt describing the disease pathway, practically compressing years of drug R&D into a few minutes on a computer. However, this vision is bottlenecked by AI's ability to predict critical drug properties like potency, toxicity, etc., based solely on its molecular structure.

Furthermore, traditional structure‑based discovery is often slowed early by the determination of reliable 3D structures. Three‑dimensional molecular structure dictates a molecule’s functionality, dynamics and interactions, which is especially important when a potential drug candidate is expected to bind to a human protein target.

Experimental methods, such as X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM, require extensive time and investment, and many promising disease targets still lack experimentally validated structural information. Computer simulations have helped lower the barrier of getting 3D structures and predicting binding affinity. However, earlier generations of algorithms for protein folding and docking (like AlphaFold and Vina respectively) only predict static snapshots of molecules and proteins (which, in reality, are inherently dynamic and shape-changing).

SAIR solves that constraint by compiling over 1 million unique computationally co-folded protein–ligand pairs, ultimately yielding 5.24 million distinct 3D complexes (five different co-folded structures per pair). Each structure is paired with a curated IC₅₀ measurement from ChEMBL or BindingDB, providing for the first time a scalable link between high-quality 3D structures and drug potency, and bridging the historic data gap that has hindered AI-driven discovery. Deep-learned affinity models such as Boltz-2, trained on similar data, have been shown to yield up to a 1,000x speed-up over the traditional, first-principle approach.

Creating SAIR was a major feat of high-performance AI computing. It took more than 130,000 GPU hours to compute the SAIR dataset using Boltz1, a cofolding AI model, on a cluster of 760 NVIDIA H100 processors, leveraging the NVIDIA DGX Cloud through Google Cloud Platform.

Capturing highly granular node, operator, scheduler, and GPU metrics, as well as a close collaboration on both infrastructure and workload optimization, helped NVIDIA AI Accelerator and SandboxAQ engineering teams identify bottlenecks and optimize configurations to achieve the highest workload throughput.

According to recent reports, consequently, the two teams were able to achieve > 95% GPU compute utilization for generating the SAIR dataset. This enabled us to create SAIR in three weeks – as opposed to the original estimate of three months (more than a 4X speed up) – and resulted in a highly optimized, GPU-native computational workflow that seamlessly integrates with today’s cutting-edge enterprise compute environments.

Generating such a massive volume of data is only half the story. Equally important is confidence in its quality, which is why every predicted complex underwent rigorous validation with PoseBusters, an industry-standard, open-source tool for benchmarking structure-related AI in drug discovery. This tool checks chemical sanity and physical plausibility.

In a recent development, the end result was that 97 percent of SAIR’s structures passed all checks. In addition to PoseBusters validation, we benchmarked leading affinity prediction methods, such as empirical scoring functions, 3D CNNs, and graph neural networks, across SAIR’s synthetic structures and experimental IC₅₀ values. The detailed results of these studies are available in our scientific manuscript on bioRxiv.

SAIR data is a reliable foundation for benchmarking latest models as well as downstream modelling, screening, and design.

In a recent development, A persistent challenge in drug discovery is the “dark proteome,” or disease‑relevant proteins for which experimental structures simply do not exist. SAIR illuminates these uncharted regions by providing credible, AI‑predicted complexes wherever experimental data is scarce. For example, more than 40 percent of the proteins in the SAIR dataset have no available structures in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) whatsoever, with or without a ligand. SAIR addresses one of the biggest challenges with existing AI models, low generalizability due to data scarcity. With SAIR, scientists can now explore targets that were previously deemed undruggable, armed with structural hypotheses to guide virtual screening and lead optimization using trustworthy model predictions.

Sources indicate that moreover, SAIR’s cross‑target breadth uncovers polypharmacology patterns and elucidates how a single molecule might interact with multiple proteins. Leveraging this rich tapestry of interactions, you can train AI models to predict off‑target effects or identify new repurposing opportunities, equipping your organization with a deeper understanding of compound profiles before any lab work begins.

SAIR is freely available on Hugging Face. Here’s a quick guide to pull SAIR from Hugging Face, peek at the main table, and (optionally) download a few structure archives.

We use the Hub to fetch files and pandas+pyarrow to read the Parquet.

This grabs the file from the Hub and loads it into a DataFrame.

Structure files are shipped as many .tar.gz archives under structures_compressed/. List them and pick what you need.

Sources indicate that each archive can be large (≈10 GB). Download only the ones you need and extract them locally.

A full version of this script, including more robust logging and validation, is available in the README file for your convenience. For more details, visit the SAIR homepage, read our manuscript on bioRxiv, or watch our 25-minute joint webinar with NVIDIA, where we demonstrate SAIR and explain how data is structured within it. Extensive documentation, tutorials, and example benchmarks are available to facilitate its use and accelerate internal adoption.The future of drug discovery is data-driven, AI-accelerated, and grounded in scalable, high-quality structural insights. While we don’t yet have AI that can design effective drug therapies with just a prompt, SAIR brings researchers ever closer to that goal with upcoming data and insights that can potentially shave years from even AI-accelerated R&D pipelines.We can’t wait to see what researchers will build using SAIR, and SandboxAQ experts are here to support them throughout the discovery process.

Contact the authors or post on the SAIR dataset discussion page.

Authors: Arman Zaribafiyan, Georgia Channing, Zane Beckwith, and Rudi Plesch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xiaomi is pushing the limits of modern smartphone specs with a killer design, flush camera lenses, and a next-gen Snapdragon SoC.

If you’re looking for a phone with top-tier specs, Xiaomi has a newly introduced phone for you. The Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max are the company’s latest flagships, available starting today, November 17. When looking at the spec list for the Xiaomi 18 series, it’s difficult to find anything that was left out.

According to recent reports, during the launch presentation, Xiaomi emphasized that its new privacy display wasn’t just a copy of “other privacy displays.” Rather, they created an entirely new subpixel layout called HyperRGB 2.0 that delivers far higher resolution and brightness output than the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. You can also enable and disable the privacy display feature on the Xiaomi 18 Pro series with a click of the new AI button on the left side of the phone. Functionally, Xiaomi’s privacy display looks nearly identical to Samsung’s, including the ability to have specific apps use it.

Sources indicate that both models feature identical specs, including the privacy display and cameras, with the exception of the screen size, battery capacity, and charging speed. Here are the differences:.

Recent findings suggest that the 120Hz LTPO display is bordered by a 0.99mm bezel, the smallest in the industry so far, 4,000-nit peak brightness, and TÜV Rheinland Triple Eye Care Certification, including a 2160Hz PWM dimming rate. Inside the phone is a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 processor with a 3D IceLoop cooling system, and each model’s silicon-carbon battery includes 28% silicon content.

In a recent development, on the back is a pair of 200MP cameras, including a 1/1.28-inch main sensor and a 1/1.56-inch periscope telephoto sensor. These are massive sensors, especially compared to the 1/3.94″ and 1/2.52″ telephoto sensors in the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Despite their size, Xiaomi packs them onto the back in an island with fully flat glass — no protruding camera lenses!

That island on the back isn’t just for cameras, though. It also packs in a 120Hz LTPO M11 OLED panel with 4,000-nit peak brightness for ultra-high-quality selfies and group shots, plus support for notifications and apps. Xiaomi created a fresh GenAI Apps feature that lets you create your own apps on the back display, plus official support for several popular apps like Google Maps, Spotify, and more.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro series ships with HyperOS 4 (Android 17) and includes 3 months of Google AI Pro, plus 5TB of Google Cloud storage. The Xiaomi 18 Pro retails for €1399 for the model with 12GB RAM and 256GB storage, or €1599 for 12GB/512GB. The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at €1599 for 12GB/256GB, €1799 for 12GB/512GB, and a 16GB/1TB model will be available soon for €2099.

Recent findings suggest that some retailers also sell a bundle that includes the Official silicone magnetic case, which usually retails for €39, as well as the Magnetic Remote Stand, which retails for €69. That remote stand functions as a MagSafe-style stand and remote, giving you camera shutter functionality and a scrolling feature.

#57829. The Downfall of Jensen Huang — a timeline of allegations and scandals that brought down the king of AI infrastructure

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2537 w)

The Downfall of Jensen Huang — a timeline of allegations and scandals that brought down the king of AI infrastructure

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2537 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia rose from a niche gaming hardware tech giant with an unofficial motto of "Our company is thirty days from going out of business” to becoming the world’s most valuable company by market capitalization in 2024, and co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang was the man behind its meteoric rise.
  • Recent findings suggest that he planned and founded the company in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem while sitting inside a Denny’s diner in the Silicon Valley area.
  • According to recent reports, all this came crumbling down for the billionaire founder in a matter of weeks, but the cracks started long before the first accusation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia rose from a niche gaming hardware tech giant with an unofficial motto of "Our company is thirty days from going out of business” to becoming the world’s most valuable company by market capitalization in 2024, and co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang was the man behind its meteoric rise.

Recent findings suggest that he planned and founded the company in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem while sitting inside a Denny’s diner in the Silicon Valley area. After more than 30 years, Nvidia had thousands of employees, a global footprint, and a name that people equated to AI chips.

According to recent reports, all this came crumbling down for the billionaire founder in a matter of weeks, but the cracks started long before the first accusation. Let’s go back and see how it all began. This is an ongoing saga, so we have listed stories related to the scandal below, which we will update as events unfold.

Jensen resigned from Nvidia on November 12, after two weeks of news reports accusing him of multiple affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with his own subordinate. This is significant for Nvidia, which has had a single CEO since its inception. Huang was the face of the company, and many of its employees, shareholders, partners, and fans still support him despite the circumstances of his departure. He steered Nvidia into the giant that it is today by having the vision to develop CUDA nearly 20 years before ChatGPT made AI accessible to the average user and buying companies that helped it scale deployments to hundreds of thousands of AI GPUs.

By 2022, ChatGPT’s arrival and subsequent boom set the AI race in motion, with tech giants and AI startups buying up as many GPUs as they could get their hands on. The increased demand for Nvidia’s products caused it to break the trillion-dollar mark in less than a year after the release of OpenAI’s LLM. As the largest individual shareholders of the tech giant, Huang and his wife, Lori, became some of the wealthiest people in the world.

In a recent development, the billionaire founder hasn't always gloated about his position. He once said in a podcast that if he could turn back time, he wouldn’t have founded Nvidia at all, and also cringed at the praises that the Caltech Board of Trustees chairperson heaped on him before he gave the 2024 keynote speech at the institute’s commencement exercises. He has frequently cited his history working as a “Dishwasher, Busboy, Waiter” at Denny’s, noting it under his experience on his LinkedIn page. More than that, people have seen Jensen go where other celebrity CEOs are rarely seen — enjoying street food in Vietnam, dining at a local fried chicken joint in Korea, and even dragging along 35 of Taiwan’s semiconductor CEOs to a restaurant in Taipei.

According to recent reports, but even as he’s building his “Man of the People” persona, his position as the head of arguably the most important chipmaker in the AI industry meant that he was also gaining influence in business and governance. Industry leaders noticed the power that Nvidia held over those who want GPUs to train their AI models, with some of his fellow billionaires begging him over dinner to sell them GPUs. Just weeks into President Donald Trump’s second term, Jensen Huang was meeting with him at the White House, discussing AI policy and hardware export controls — something the Biden administration started in 2022 in an attempt to hold back China’s ambition'sin AI.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

In a recent development, the rivalry between the U.S. and China has been simmering for years, with Chinese companies like Huawei getting blacklisted because of their work with the People’s Liberation Army. In August 2022, about three months before ChatGPT made AI a household term, Washington expanded its trade bans on Beijing and imposed export controls on Nvidia’s H100 and A100 GPUs. The tech giant responded to this by building a fresh data center GPU that conformed to U.S. standards specifically for the Chinese market, called the A800, by November of that year. Despite delivering only 70% of the performance of the A100 it was based on, the GPU reportedly still saw great demand from Chinese customers.

It has been revealed that however, the A800 only had a relatively short run as the Biden administration once again increased the performance threshold in October 2023, which resulted in the export prohibition of A800 and H800 GPUs to China. This move forced the organization to iterate once again, creating new models that it could sell to Chinese companies, like the Nvidia H20. These chips arrived on the market in early 2024, but before the Biden administration ended in January 2025, it proposed even stricter rules called the AI Diffusion Policy. This sorted nations into different tiers based on trust and risk levels — countries in tier 1, which includes the U.S. and its closest allies, have minimal restrictions, while those in tier 3 are effectively barred from receiving advanced AI GPUs containing U.S. technology.

According to recent reports, this is problematic for Nvidia, as China is the second-largest computer market in the world t and represented between 20% and 25% of Nvidia's data center sales. The tech giant lobbied the U.S. government to ease AI GPU export restrictions, with Trump reportedly suspending the proposed Nvidia H20 ban after Jensen spent $1 million to have dinner with the president in early April 2025. The White House went ahead anyway and banned the sale of the AI GPU less than a week after that, resulting in a $5.5 billion write-off for the company.

Jensen Huang himself had harsh comments about Washington’s trade ban, saying that “export control was a failure,” and that it had caused the firm’s AI GPU market share in China to go from 95% to zero. He even argued that “conceding an entire market the size of China probably does not make a lot of strategic sense, so I think that has already largely backfired.”.

Sources indicate that but even as Huang was fighting to have the trade ban on the Nvidia H20 chip lifted, he continued praising Trump’s tariff plan, calling it “utterly visionary.” The president eventually reversed the ban three months later, and by December 2025, he had approved Nvidia H200 exports to China, but only if Nvidia pays a 25% fee. The newer Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips remain out of reach for Chinese companies, though — at least on paper.

Industry observers note that allegations that Chinese companies have been breaking Washington’s trade ban and smuggling Nvidia AI GPUs into China have been circulating since June 2023, after Reuters revealed that vendors in Shenzhen could secure A100 chips when asked discreetly. They reportedly bought these chips from the excess stocks sold in the open market or through intermediaries in India, Taiwan, and Singapore. Another story published in January 2024 asserted that the Chinese military and related institutions, state-run data centers, and even universities continue buying banned A100 and H100 chips. Six months after that, accounts of underground networks dedicated to smuggling AI GPUs — even entire servers — through other countries started emerging.

According to recent reports, in 2025, an investigative report revealed that at least a billion dollars’ worth of Nvidia AI chips were allegedly funneled into China. Some sellers likened the illicit AI GPU trade to a seafood market, with brokers and retailers openly advertising the most advanced Nvidia AI chips online, from RTX 5090 GPUs to complete B200 servers.

It has been revealed that even with all these reports, Huang continued denying that Nvidia’s chips were being smuggled into China. “There’s no evidence of any AI chip diversion,” the then-CEO told reporters at Computex 2025. He also added, “The Grace Blackwell system is nearly two tons, and so you’re not going to be shipping — you’re not going to be putting that in your pocket or your backpack anytime soon. And so, these systems are fairly easy to keep track of... but the crucial thing is that the countries and the companies that we sell to recognize that diversion is not allowed, and everybody would like to continue to buy Nvidia technology, and so they very well monitor themselves very carefully and they’re quite careful about that.”.

In the midst of all these AI chip smuggling rumors, the Bureau of Industry and Security, the agency in charge of enforcing U.S. trade sanctions, was found to be “inadequate” and underfunded, and it has been relying on outdated manual processes to enforce restrictions on Chinese tech companies. Despite that, companies and individuals across the world are being investigated and arrested for bypassing Washington’s export controls.

Singaporean authorities broke up a smuggling ring in early 2025 that smuggled Nvidia GPUs for Chinese AI lab DeepSeek, resulting in a raid of 22 different locations and the arrest of nine people. In October of the same year, a Singapore tech giant called Megaspeed, which was led by Alice Huang, allegedly diverted $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips. Four Americans were then arrested the following month for shipping 400 Nvidia A100s and attempting to send 50 more Nvidia H200 GPUs to China.

An even bigger smuggling scandal unfolded some four months after the arrests, after three Super Micro employees were arrested for smuggling $2.5 billion of Nvidia hardware into China. The suspects included firm co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, although Super Micro itself was not implicated. The Super Micro case spanned the globe, with Taiwanese authorities raiding 12 locations related to the case in May 2026, with another nine sites and six people investigated in June. Jensen Huang urged the company to fix its export control compliance after the arrests and raids, telling the media, “We insist our partners are compliant. We hope that they will enhance and improve their regulatory compliance and prevent that from happening in the future.”.

But just five months after he made this statement, one stunning accusation unraveled it all.

On October 29, 2026, The New York Times published a report that Jensen Huang may have been the target of a Chinese spy plot through the executive of a firm who was “close” to him — that executive is Alice Huang. Nvidia denied the accusation. “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” a company spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. “Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security.".

But a little over a week later, U.S. intelligence sources claimed that the former Nvidia chief had an affair with the Megaspeed executive. This is the same Megaspeed that has been accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to the tune of $2 billion. By the evening of Sunday, November 8, Jensen admitted to the affair, although he did not name the third party in his statement.

Sources indicate that many government officials would usually turn a blind eye towards a tech executive’s personal life, but the fact that he is the leader of the U.S.’s premier AI chip maker and that he is also close to the president has caught the attention of authorities. This has led to the U.S. Congress asking him to a closed-door meeting to discuss Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” and the FBI investigating his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy.

In a recent development, the admission and allegations led to people digging deeper into Alice Huang. An investigation by The Information revealed that she was connected to a “labyrinth” of companies spanning Singapore, China, and the British Virgin Islands, and that she allegedly helped move around $7.5 billion worth of AI GPU imports. $2 billion was routed from Megaspeed to Speedmatrix, its Malaysia subsidiary, while another $4.6 billion moved directly from the Singaporean company into Shanghai Century Litong, a China-based cloud services company. It has also reportedly bought Nvidia GPUs from other sources, resulting in the estimated total value of its imports.

Recent findings suggest that people close to her also stated that she would leverage her relationship with Jensen to customers, often posting pictures with him on her WeChat account, showing potential clients unpublished photos with the Nvidia chief, and even boasting that he would take her to dinner and give her gifts on her birthday. It also seems that Alice Huang was not acting alone. Multiple sources say that Kang Wei, Alice Huang’s husband, was central to the operation to acquire AI GPUs. He even seemingly acknowledged her relationship with Jensen Huang and has jokingly said that she was a personal assistant to the billionaire.

However, it seems that the straw that broke the camel’s back was another allegation that Jensen had an affair with another woman — this time, with Kimberly Powell, the organization’s vice president of health care who directly reported to him. Hours after this revelation, the company board announced that Jensen had resigned from all his leadership positions at Nvidia, with employees saying he looked “broken and shattered” as he left the company he spent over three decades building in disgrace. Nvidia is looking for internal and external CEO candidates. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim chief executive.

It may be the end of an era, but this does not necessarily spell the end for Jensen Huang. Despite his sudden downfall and quick removal from Nvidia, his status as the king of AI infrastructure remains valuable to the AI industry. Elon Musk even mentioned on X that it “would be an honor” to hire him, and this could ring true for any business that wants to break into the semiconductor space. But does he even want to return?Huang's first public statement after his resignation came on X on Nov. 17, in which the former CEO said he has "outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," and that if asked by the company's board, he would be "honored" to take the job.".

Sources indicate that over 190,000 shareholders, partners, current and former employees, and fans, including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, have signed an online petition to bring him back as the leader of the firm. President Donald Trump called for his reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.The board, however, may not see things the same way. Multiple reports suggest that the board isn't considering bringing Huang back, and instead is focusing on a new candidate, the ongoing investigation into Huang, and preparing for national security investigations.

Welcome EmbeddingGemma, Google's upcoming efficient embedding model

📅 04 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2734 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, today, Google releases EmbeddingGemma, a state-of-the-art multilingual embedding model perfect for on-device use cases.
  • Text embeddings have become the backbone of modern natural‑language applications, turning words, sentences, and documents into dense vectors that capture meaning, sentiment, and intent.
  • Building on this foundation, Google DeepMind’s EmbeddingGemma arrives as the newest, most capable small multilingual embedding model yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, today, Google releases EmbeddingGemma, a state-of-the-art multilingual embedding model perfect for on-device use cases. Designed for speed and efficiency, the model features a compact size of 308M parameters and a 2K context window, unlocking new possibilities for mobile RAG pipelines, agents, and more. EmbeddingGemma is trained to support over 100 languages and is the highest-ranking text-only multilingual embedding model under 500M on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) at the time of writing.

Text embeddings have become the backbone of modern natural‑language applications, turning words, sentences, and documents into dense vectors that capture meaning, sentiment, and intent. These vectors enable fast similarity search, clustering, classification, and retrieval across massive corpora, powering everything from recommendation engines and semantic search to retrieval-augmented generation and code‑search tools. Embedding models that calculate these embeddings are widely used, with well over 200 million monthly downloads on Hugging Face.

Building on this foundation, Google DeepMind’s EmbeddingGemma arrives as the newest, most capable small multilingual embedding model yet. With just 308M parameters, a 2k‑token context window, and support for over 100 languages, EmbeddingGemma delivers state‑of‑the‑art performance on the Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark (MMTEB) while staying under 200 MB of RAM when quantized.

The various design choices result in a very practical, open-source tool for computing high-quality multilingual embeddings on everyday devices.

In this blogpost, we describe the EmbeddingGemma architecture and training, and show you how to use the model with various frameworks like Sentence Transformers, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, txtai, Transformers.js, Text Embedding Inference, and ONNX.

Sources indicate that afterwards, we demonstrate how to finetune EmbeddingGemma on your domain for even stronger performance. In our example, we finetune EmbeddingGemma on the Medical Instruction and Retrieval Dataset (MIRIAD). The resulting model, sentence-transformers/embeddinggemma-300m-medical, achieves state-of-the-art performance on our task: retrieving passages of scientific medical papers in response to detailed medical questions. It even outperforms models twice as massive on this task.

EmbeddingGemma builds on the Gemma3 transformers backbone, but modified to use bi-directional attention instead of causal (one-way) attention. This means that earlier tokens in the sequence can attend to later tokens, effectively turning the architecture from a decoder into an encoder. Encoder models can outperform LLMs, which are decoders, on embedding tasks like retrieval (Weller et al., 2025). With this backbone, the model can process a sizable 2048 tokens at once, sufficient for typical retrieval inputs, especially given that larger inputs often result in information loss in the text embeddings.

Industry observers note that beyond the upcoming Gemma3-based encoder backbone, which produces token embeddings, a mean pooling layer converts these token embeddings into text embeddings. Lastly, two dense layers transform the text embeddings into their final form, a 768-dimensional vector.

Recent findings suggest that the EmbeddingGemma model has been trained with Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), allowing you to truncate the 768‑dimensional output to 512, 256, or 128 dimensions on demand. This results in faster downstream processing and lower memory and disk space utilization. See the Sentence Transformers usage for a snippet showing how to perform this truncation.

It has been revealed that the model has been trained using a carefully curated, multilingual corpus totalling approximately 320 billion tokens. The proprietary dataset is a blend of publicly available web text, code and technical documentation, and synthetic task‑specific examples. It has been filtered to avoid Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM), sensitive data, and low-quality or unsafe content.

EmbeddingGemma was benchmarked on the MMTEB (Multilingual, v2) and MTEB (English, v2) suites, which span a wide range of tasks, domains, and languages. Despite its modest 308M‑parameter size, the model consistently beats comparable baselines while keeping a very small memory footprint.

Recent findings suggest that the results will be listed on the official MTEB Leaderboard. We exclude any model that has been trained on more than 20% of the MTEB data, to mitigate potential over‑fitting.

The demo can also be experienced in full screen.

Experience the demo yourself on a Desktop device.

EmbeddingGemma is integrated with many popular tools, making it easy to incorporate into your existing workflows and applications. The model has been integrated in Sentence Transformers, and thus also in projects that use Sentence Transformers behind the scenes, such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, and txtai. See the examples below to get started with your preferred framework.

For production deployments, you can use Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) to serve the model efficiently on various hardware configurations, and you can use Transformers.js for use in web applications.

Recent findings suggest that regardless of your framework choice, you should be mindful of the prompts. For embedding models, prompts are prepended to the input text to allow the model to distinguish between different tasks. Because google/embeddinggemma-300m was trained with MRL, the embeddings generated by this model can be truncated to lower dimensionalities without considerably hurting the evaluation performance. Embeddings with lower dimensionalities are both cheaper to store on disk and in memory, as well as faster for downstream tasks like retrieval, clustering, or classification.

In Sentence Transformers, you can set a lower dimensionality using the truncate_dim parameter on either the SentenceTransformer initialization or when calling model.encode/model.encode_query/model.encode_document:.

Note that the ranking is preserved despite using 3x smaller embeddings compared to the full-sized embeddings.

In a recent development, if you prefer, you can also use the LangChain HuggingFaceEmbeddings, which uses Sentence Transformers behind the scenes. Note that you'll have to tell LangChain to use the prompts called "query" and "document" for queries and documents, respectively. You can easily deploy EmbeddingGemma for both development and production using Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) version 1.8.1 or later.

If you run the Docker container with the cuda-1.8.1 tag, it includes support for multiple GPU architectures: Turing, Ampere, Ada Lovelace, and Hopper. For a lighter image tailored to just your GPU, you can instead use a specific tag such as turing-1.8.1, 1.8.1 and 86-1.8.1 (Ampere), 89-1.8.1 (Ada Lovelace), or hopper-1.8.1.

Once deployed, regardless of the device or runtime, you can leverage the /v1/embeddings endpoint based on the OpenAI Embeddings API Specification to generate embeddings.

Alternatively, you can also leverage the /embed endpoint from the Text Embeddings Inference Embeddings API, which supports the prompt_name parameter, meaning there’s no need to manually prepend the prompt to the inputs but select it via prompt_name instead.

Additionally, note that since google/embeddinggemma-300m was trained with Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), you can also leverage the dimensions parameter, on both /v1/embeddings and /embed, to truncate the embeddings to lower dimensionalities (512, 256, and 128) without hurting the evaluation performance.

In a recent development, you can also run the model directly with ONNX Runtime, making it highly portable and cross-platform compatible. The example below highlights usage in Python, but the same approach can be applied in other languages (Java, C#, C++, etc.) as well.

In a recent development, as with all models compatible with the Sentence Transformers library, EmbeddingGemma can be easily fine-tuned on your specific dataset. To showcase this, we'll be finetuning google/embeddinggemma-300m on the Medical Instruction and RetrIeval Dataset (MIRIAD) dataset, such that our finetuned model becomes particularly adept at finding passages up to 1000 tokens from scientific medical papers given detailed medical questions. These passages can be used as crucial context for a generative model to answer questions more effectively.

Sources indicate that below, you can explore each key component of the finetuning process using expandable tabs. Each tab contains the relevant code and a detailed explanation.

This code loads the EmbeddingGemma model from Hugging Face, with optional model card metadata for documentation and sharing. The SentenceTransformer class loads the model weights and configuration, while the model_card_data argument attaches metadata useful for inclusion in the automatically generated model card.

This code loads the MIRIAD dataset, or rather, a copy that has been divided into train, eval, and test splits. Using a large, high-quality dataset ensures the model learns meaningful representations, while subsetting allows for faster experimentation. The load_dataset function fetches the dataset from Hugging Face Datasets, and the .select() method limits the number of samples for each split.

This code defines the loss function for training, using Cached Multiple Negatives Ranking Loss (CMNRL). CMNRL is effective for retrieval tasks, as it uses in-batch negatives to efficiently train the model to distinguish between correct and incorrect pairs. The loss takes question-answer pairs and treats other answers in the batch as negatives, maximizing the distance between unrelated pairs in the embedding space. The mini_batch_size parameter controls the memory usage, but does not affect the training dynamics.

According to recent reports, it's recommended to use this loss with a large per_device_train_batch_size in SentenceTransformerTrainingArguments and a low mini_batch_size in CachedMultipleNegativesRankingLoss for a strong training signal with low memory usage. Additionally, the NO_DUPLICATES batch sampler is recommended to avoid accidental false negatives.

This code sets up all hyperparameters and configuration for training, evaluation, and logging. Proper training arguments are crucial for efficient, stable, and reproducible training. The arguments control batch sizes, learning rate, mixed precision, evaluation and saving frequency, and more. Notably, the prompts dictionary maps dataset columns to prompts used by the model to distinguish queries from documents.

In a recent development, this code sets up an evaluator for information retrieval, using queries and a corpus to measure model performance. Evaluation during training helps monitor progress and avoid overfitting. The evaluator computes retrieval metrics (NDCG, MRR, Recall, Precision, MAP, etc.) by checking if the model retrieves the correct passages for each query. It can be run before, during, and after training, and the results will be logged and incorporated in the automatically generated model card.

Note that this snippet in particular uses all (1k) evaluation questions against a corpus of all (1k) evaluation passages and 30k training passages, for a total of 31k documents. Evaluating only against evaluation passages is too simple for the model.

This code initializes and runs the training loop, coordinating all components.

The performance of the base model was already excellent, with a strong 0.8340 NDCG@10 on our MIRIAD test set. Despite that, we were able to increase it considerably on this domain-specific dataset.

Sources indicate that our fine-tuning process achieved a significant improvement of +0.0522 NDCG@10 on the test set, resulting in a model that comfortably outperforms any existing general-purpose embedding model on our specific task, at this model size. Additional time and compute investment would allow for even stronger results, such as hard negatives mining or training with more than 100k data pairs.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A chemical spill at a SpaceXAI facility in Southaven saw the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) get involved, with between 5,000 and 6,000 gallons of propylene glycol confirmed to have spilled.
  • However, it has also been confirmed that water samples will be collected for further laboratory analysis while workers continue to clean the area and monitor for any further problems.
  • Sources indicate that it hasn't been a great November for SpaceXAI in Southaven.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A chemical spill at a SpaceXAI facility in Southaven saw the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) get involved, with between 5,000 and 6,000 gallons of propylene glycol confirmed to have spilled. The chemical is a heat transfer fluid used in a variety of products, such as antifreeze. The chemical ultimately found its way into a drainage ditch, but MDEQ has told residents that there is no immediate threat to their health or safety, according to local news reports.

However, it has also been confirmed that water samples will be collected for further laboratory analysis while workers continue to clean the area and monitor for any further problems. It's also been reported that the chemical was contained to the drainage ditch and did not reach the nearby Horn Lake Creek.

Sources indicate that it hasn't been a great November for SpaceXAI in Southaven. Earlier this month, it suffered a setback in a lawsuit over pollution in the area caused by its data center. The April 2026 suit targets the company's gas-powered power plant, which is used to supply power for its facility in the Greater Memphis area. It's argued that 27 gas turbines were installed without obtaining the required permits. It's also alleged that the plant could emit more than 5,000 tons of nitrogen oxides and 47 tons of formaldehyde — a cancer-causing chemical — annually. The company has tried to classify the turbines as mobile units to get around the concern, but a judge rejected that manoeuvre.

Clearly aware of the local sentiment towards its presence, SpaceXAI offered a 50% Starlink discount to anyone living near its two Memphis data centers. It also said that it would waive the hardware cost, saving customers $349. SpaceXAI said that, between late June and early September, around 2,000 residents of the greater Memphis and Southaven area had signed up for Starlink connectivity.

Sources indicate that it was also recently declared that the City of Memphis was ready to make its first major investment as part of its upcoming Community Benefits Ordinance, a fund that uses revenue from SpaceXAI's Colossus 1 facility. Almost $3.3 million will be pumped back into the city to help with housing and neighborhood improvements.

The Pixel Tag will begin selling in Europe soon, according to a recent leak. The Android Find Hub tracker sold nearly everywhere else during the initial launch.

In a recent development, google’s very first tracker joined the dozens of other options that work on the Android Find Hub network, launching alongside the Pixel 11 earlier in the year. It’s a sleek little tracking tag, with some first-party care that makes it stand out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that one criticism that has emerged of Nvidia’s Vera CPU, driven by AMD, is that Nvidia – and, to a lesser degree, Arm with its AGI CPU – couldn’t have developed an “agentic CPU,” as the chip is often characterized in Nvidia’s marketing materials. Ian Finder, the head of Nvidia’s data center CPU business, pushed back on that criticism in a recent conversation with Tom’s Hardware Premium at SC26, calling the notion that Nvidia somehow knew about the agentic wave four years ago when Vera development began "absurd.".

“There's a conviction around the design philosophy of the part, right? Am I going to sit here and tell you that we have this magic crystal ball around the agentic moment? That would be absurd, right?” Finder said. “But what we do have as a organization, and I think this has been proven out in our track record, is [that] we have design intuition.”.

Instead of specifically designing Vera for agentic workloads, which would be impossible without a way to see several years into the future, Finder characterized the part by its codesign with Nvidia’s accelerators, something that the team has continued to work on since its first Grace data center CPU. Coming from the assumption that data centers and AI workloads are accelerated (and they largely are), Finder says the co-design approach on the CPU can start in a “conceptually simple space, like what kind of CPU do we need to keep the accelerator fed and happy?”.

Sources indicate that although conceptually simple, Finder continually looped back to a particular word to describe aspects of Vera and, to a lesser extent, Grace. “Opinionated” is the word he used, which in the broader context of Vera’s design, demonstrates up in two places. Grace, Finder says, introduced an opinionated memory system with Nvidia’s Scalable Coherency Fabric, while Vera extends that memory system while adding an opinionated microarchitecture, Nvidia’s Olympus core.

In a recent development, the picture Finder paints is one of Nvidia starting from scratch in this space, contrasting it with the “legacy constraints” of, presumably, Intel and AMD in particular, who have large pools of customers with specific needs. As we described in our original breakdown of the Olympus architecture in Vera, Nvidia’s goal doesn’t seem to be to steal market share from AMD and Intel, but rather to grab market share in a CPU space that’s vastly accelerating on the back of AI agents.

Industry observers note that this “clean sheet of paper” approach, and Nvidia’s codesign, led to some natural assumptions about what the CPU should do. “If we have silicon that needs really, really great single-thread performance, [and] we also need concurrency, then we need to get there with IPC instead of frequency. We need to make sure we have good loaded memory latency. We need to make sure we have a lot of bandwidth, and you start to design something on a clean sheet of paper that's not encumbered by dollar-per-core economics.”.

Recent findings suggest that although Finder was clear that Vera’s design didn’t explicitly center around the agents we see today, there were early indications of the workload. “To say that four years ago, when we started putting pen to paper on Vera, [that] we absolutely saw the agentic moment, would [not] be... something I would claim, but we were starting to see the beginnings of tool calling and things like that. We certainly knew what we needed from a head node, and we knew the overall shape of this problem.”.

As you can see in our Vera CPU benchmarking, the chip doesn’t excel at every workload. And, from the data you can see in our recent AMD EPYC Venice benchmarking, the AMD camp has reclaimed some top spots in several benchmarks. Finder suggests that the superior memory bandwidth of Vera will play a much bigger role in the agentic future as these systems evolve to take better advantage of the compute available.

A portion of the AI industry is focused on tackling the problem of fully utilizing the GPU, Nvidia included. GPUs shouldn’t sit idle for very long (if at all) with the demand today, and they don’t. The challenge today is spinning up these agent sandboxes quickly, within milliseconds, so that the CPU isn’t sitting idle, either.

Sources indicate that finder provided an example of using a coding agent. If you’ve used a coding agent before, you’re probably familiar with this process. After prompting, the model will make several small tool calls to read and locate files, passing back to the model in between. These are tiny calls, almost negligible, and the vast majority of the time is spent in the model on the GPU. Then, it may start compiling and testing the project, which is much more bound by the CPU. The GPU, Finder says, isn't sitting idle during that time. It’s being leveraged for another purpose. Finder suggests “that very same thing is going to happen on the CPU.”.

According to recent reports, this “very interesting computer science problem,” as Finder described it, is being investigated by AI startups such as Daytona and E2B to spin up and close down agentic sandboxes in milliseconds. And serving more agents will naturally put pressure on the memory system, which is an area where Vera has an edge. “We built a product that does really, really well without such optimizations, but as a design point that really will lean into them when the industry starts to catch up to this,” Finder remarked.

Industry observers note that vera is a fascinating chip, regardless of what you think of it and how it’s presented in marketing materials (from Nvidia itself or elsewhere). Although Grace was the starting point internally, Vera has ridden the wave of agentic to become a much bigger player in the world of CPUs, and Nvidia has already unveiled that it will follow up with its Rosa CPU featuring the newly introduced Rigel microarchitecture. Vera is an opinionated CPU indeed, and time will tell if that opinion is correct.

Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

mmBERT: ModernBERT goes Multilingual

📅 09 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1333 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This blog post introduces mmBERT, a state-of-the-art massively multilingual encoder model trained on 3T+ tokens of text in over 1800 languages.
  • If you are interested in trying out the models yourself, some example boilerplate is available at the end of this blogpost!
  • Industry observers note that mmBERT was trained on a carefully curated multilingual dataset totaling over 3T tokens across three distinct training phases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This blog post introduces mmBERT, a state-of-the-art massively multilingual encoder model trained on 3T+ tokens of text in over 1800 languages. It reveals significant performance and speed improvements over previous multilingual models, being the first to improve upon XLM-R, while also developing new strategies for effectively learning low-resource languages. mmBERT builds upon ModernBERT for a blazingly fast architecture, and adds novel components to enable efficient multilingual learning.

If you are interested in trying out the models yourself, some example boilerplate is available at the end of this blogpost!

Industry observers note that mmBERT was trained on a carefully curated multilingual dataset totaling over 3T tokens across three distinct training phases. The foundation of our training data consists of three primary open-source and high-quality web crawls that enable both multilingual coverage and data quality:.

DCLM and Filtered DCLM provides the highest quality English content available, serving as the backbone for strong English performance (with the filtered data coming from Dolmino). This dataset represents state-of-the-art web filtering techniques and forms a crucial component. Due to the high quality of this data, we use a signficantly higher proportion of English than previous generation multilingual encoder models (up to 18%).

FineWeb2 delivers broad multilingual web content covering over 1,800 languages. This dataset enables our extensive multilingual coverage while maintaining reasonable quality standards across diverse language families and scripts.

FineWeb2-HQ consists of a filtered subset of FineWeb2 focusing on 20 high-resource languages. This filtered version provides higher-quality multilingual content that bridges the gap between English-only filtered data and broad multilingual coverage.

The training data also incorporates specialized corpora from Dolma, MegaWika v2, ProLong and more: code repositories (StarCoder, ProLong), academic content (ArXiv, PeS2o), reference materials (Wikipedia, textbooks), and community discussions (StackExchange), along with instruction and mathematical datasets.

Industry observers note that the key innovation in our data approach is the progressive language inclusion strategy shown in Figure 1. At each phase we progressively sample from a flatter distribution (i.e. closer to uniform), while also adding latest languages. This means that high resource languages like Russian start off with a high percentage of the data (i.e. 9%) and then in the last phase of training end around half of that. We start with 60 high-resource languages during pre-training, expand to 110 languages during mid-training, and finally include all 1,833 languages from FineWeb2 during the decay phase. This allows us to maximize the impact of limited low-resource language data without excess reptitions and while maintaining high overall data quality.

mmBERT builds upon the ModernBERT architecture but introduces several key innovations for multilingual learning:.

We use the same core architecture as ModernBERT-base with 22 layers and 1152 intermediate dimensions, but switch to the Gemma 2 tokenizer to better handle multilingual text. The base model has 110M non-embedding parameters (307M total due to the larger vocabulary), while the small variant has 42M non-embedding parameters (140M total).

Our training follows a carefully designed three-phase schedule:.

In a recent development, inverse Mask Ratio Schedule: Instead of using a fixed masking rate, we progressively reduce the mask ratio from 30% → 15% → 5% across training phases. This allows the model to learn basic representations with higher masking early on, then focus on more nuanced understanding with lower masking rates.

Annealed Language Learning: We dynamically adjust the temperature for multilingual data sampling from τ=0.7 → 0.5 → 0.3. This creates a progression from high-resource language bias toward more uniform sampling, enabling the model to build a strong multilingual foundation before learning low-resource languages.

Industry observers note that progressive Language Addition: Rather than training on all languages simultaneously, we strategically add languages at each phase (60 → 110 → 1,833). This maximizes learning efficiency by avoiding excessive epochs on limited low-resource data while still achieving strong performance.

Model Merging: We train three different variants during the decay phase (English-focused, 110-language, and all-language) and use TIES merging to combine their strengths into the final model.

English Performance: On the English GLUE benchmark (Table 1), mmBERT base achieves strong performance, substantially outperforming other multilingual models like XLM-R (multilingual RoBERTa) base and mGTE base, while remaining competitive to English-only models despite less than 25% of the mmBERT training data being English.

It has been revealed that multilingual Performance: mmBERT demonstrates significant improvements on XTREME benchmark compared to XLM-R as demonstrated in Table 2. Notable gains include strong performance on XNLI classification, substantial improvements in question answering tasks like TyDiQA, and competitive results across PAWS-X and XCOPA for cross-lingual understanding.

Industry observers note that the model performs well across most categories, with the exception of some structured prediction tasks like NER and POS tagging, likely due to tokenizer differences that affect word boundary detection. On these categories, it performs about the same as the previous generation, but can be applied to more languages.

English Retrieval: Even though mmBERT is designed for massively multilingual settings, in the MTEB v2 English benchmarks (Table 3), mmBERT indicates significant gains over previous multilingual models and even ties the capabilities of English-only models like ModernBERT!

Multilingual Retrieval: mmBERT highlights consistent improvements on MTEB v2 multilingual benchmarks compared to other models (Table 4).

Code Retrieval: Due to the modern tokenizer (based on Gemma 2) mmBERT also shows strong coding performance (Table 5), making mmBERT suitable for any type of textual data. The only model that outperforms it is EuroBERT, which was able to use the non-publicly accessible Stack v2 dataset.

One of mmBERT's most significant novel features is demonstrating that low-resource languages can be effectively learned during the short decay phase of training. We validated this approach by testing on languages only introduced during the final 100B token decay phase.

It has been revealed that dramatic Performance Gains: Testing on TiQuaD (Tigrinya) and FoQA (Faroese), we observed substantial improvements when these languages were included in the decay phase, as shown in Figure 2. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our progressive language learning approach.

Competitive with Large Models: Despite only seeing these languages in the final training phase, mmBERT achieves performance levels that exceed much larger models. On Faroese question answering where LLMs have been benchmarked, mmBERT outperforms Google Gemini 2.5 Pro and OpenAI o3.

Rapid Learning Mechanism: The success of decay-phase language learning stems from the model's ability to leverage its strong multilingual foundation built during earlier phases. When exposed to new languages, the model can rapidly adapt existing cross-lingual representations rather than learning from scratch.

Model Merging Benefits: The final mmBERT models successfully retain most of the decay-phase improvements while benefiting from the English-focused and high-resource variants through TIES merging.

mmBERT delivers substantial efficiency gains over previous multilingual encoder models through architectural improvements inherited from ModernBERT:.

It has been revealed that throughput Performance: mmBERT processes text significantly faster than existing multilingual models across various sequence lengths, as demonstrated in Figure 3. Both the small and base models show substantial speed improvements over previous multilingual encoders.

Modern Architecture Benefits: The efficiency gains come from two main technical improvements:.

Sequence Length Scaling: Unlike older models limited to 512 tokens, mmBERT handles up to 8,192 tokens efficiently while maintaining high throughput. This makes it suitable for longer document processing tasks that are increasingly common in multilingual applications.

Energy Efficiency: The combination of better throughput and modern architecture results in lower computational costs for inference, making mmBERT more practical for production deployments where multilingual support is needed at scale.

These efficiency improvements make mmBERT not just more accurate than previous multilingual encoders, but also significantly more practical for real usage.

Internal links should not exist merely to move ranking signals around.

They should help consumers move between related tasks.

A technical guide might lead to a product page. A product page might link back to the configuration guide. A category page should make important child resources discoverable without requiring a user to know the exact URL.

Industry observers note that at a broader level, crawlability is one part of technical SEO and search visibility. A page that nobody can reliably discover is difficult to evaluate regardless of how strong its content may be.

#57819. Leaked Ohio bill could allow AI data center companies to seize private land for their buildouts using eminent domain law

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (509 w)
📖 Baca

Leaked Ohio bill could allow AI data center companies to seize private land for their buildouts using eminent domain law

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (509 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While Ohioans have rejected the building of upcoming data centers at every turn, they might not have much choice in the future.
  • According to recent reports, legal experts have warned that the change could mean a transmission developer, like a power organization, would be able to seize land to be used for a data center or a facility that would power one.
  • In a recent development, this follows a July 2026 report that the government was able to seize private land for new transmission lines needed to power new data centers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While Ohioans have rejected the building of upcoming data centers at every turn, they might not have much choice in the future. That's if a newly leaked bill that could allow data centers to be classified as public utilities is allowed to progress. The move would see the list of who can qualify for eminent domain law expanded, moving beyond entities owned or operated by municipal corporations, electric cooperatives, and agencies holding a certificate of public convenience and necessity granted by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. The bill, leaked to WCPO Cincinnati, would add "and an agency holding a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need from the power siting board for constructing an electric transmission line and associated facilities or gas pipeline and its associated facilities.".

According to recent reports, legal experts have warned that the change could mean a transmission developer, like a power organization, would be able to seize land to be used for a data center or a facility that would power one. The writing has been on the wall for a while, too, after it was discovered in June that the Ohio Business Roundtable trade group recommended that lawmakers change eminent domain law to "extend possession authority to energy infrastructure projects once public use and necessity have been established.”.

In a recent development, this follows a July 2026 report that the government was able to seize private land for new transmission lines needed to power new data centers. The law gives the government the power to take private land without the need for the owner's consent, so long as it is for public use and the owner receives appropriate compensation. The government can also delegate the same land-grabbing power to “private entities or common carriers,” which includes utility companies.

This is already happening, too. Earlier this year, the largest utility company in Georgia required the removal of 30 residential properties in order to upgrade its grid. Residents claimed that the expansion was to power AI data centers, a fact given more weight by the fact that one such data center was located just a few miles away.

Despite this, eminent domain law can still be used for good. Nashville set out to use the same law to block the building of a 69,220-square-foot single-story data center next to a zoo. Nashville Metro Council approved the use of eminent domain as a way to buy the land from a local developer who planned the $700 million data center buildout.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As previewed at I/O 2026, you can text — via Google Messages and iMessage — or email directly with Gemini.

Instead of using the Gemini app, you can now reach the AI assistant to “start tasks and get updates” using your preferred method of communication. To get started, go to gemini.google.com/channels.

You can now assign Gemini ‘tasks’ for free in six countries.

Text with Gemini works via Google Messages and iMessage. Google does note that this method is “not end-to-end encrypted and may be accessible by your carrier.” The setup process involves verifying a phone number. Existing numbers associated with your Google Account appear automatically, and there’s the ability to add a new one.

It has been revealed that afterward, you’ll receive a text from Gemini via RCS Business Messaging that offers a pretty straightforward chat experience. Before sending, booking, or other “major actions,” Gemini will ask for 1-tap confirmation.

According to recent reports, …you can text a request, snap a photo of a school flyer to add dates to your Google Calendar, or get scheduled check-ins in a private 1:1 thread. If your intends change while Gemini is working, simply reply to the text to steer the task mid-run without starting over.

(Amusingly, Text with Gemini coexists with the existing Google Messages integration, which you can distinguish by the old blue/purple icon.).

Sources indicate that email with Gemini lets you “start tasks and get updates by emailing” gemini@google.com. Google explicitly names Gmail, Apple Mail, or Outlook as supported clients, while emails from Gemini are always “1:1 to you (never “Reply-All”) with a link to review and confirm your results.”.

Forward a batch of school emails to add key dates to Google Calendar, spot schedule conflicts, or send over threads and PDFs to sort out medical bills and track insurance renewals.

You can manage phone numbers and turn off both options from this fresh Channels page. If you’re more familiar with using your email client or phone’s messaging app, Text and Email with Gemini might boost your assistant usage. This is available first in the US.

Meanwhile, when announced in May, these two options were intended for Gemini Spark, which has since been integrated into the main Gemini experience as “tasks.”.

#57817. Jupyter Agents: training LLMs to reason with notebooks

📅 10 Sep 2025 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2156 w)
